headline: Viral video: Protester threatens to kill police during Gazipur rally
summary: A participant in a Jubo League rally in Gazipur city sparked widespread criticism after a video emerged showing them threatening police officers.
details: A video circulating on social media has captured a protester making a direct threat to police officers during a rally in Gazipur city.
The incident occurred during a procession brought out in the Choydana Maleker Bari area, in front of a garment factory along the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway.
In the viral footage, one individual is heard saying, "Not a single one of you should come forward; we will kill you outright."
Eyewitnesses reported that the remark was made as police were approaching the procession to manage the situation.
Bason Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Harun Or Rashid confirmed that Jubo League leaders and activists participated in the rally.
Despite the viral video and the resulting public outcry, police have not yet detained any individuals in connection with the incident.
Local sources indicated that the rally was organized to mark the founding anniversary of the Awami League, whose activities remain banned.

headline_marked: Heavy rain forecast: [[Flood alert issued for Sylhet and north Bangladesh]]
headline: Heavy rain forecast: Flood alert issued for Sylhet and north Bangladesh
summary: The Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre warns of short-term flooding in low-lying areas as rivers in Rangpur and Sylhet divisions may exceed danger levels.
details: The Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) has warned that heavy rainfall over the coming days could trigger short-term flooding in parts of Bangladesh, despite all major rivers currently flowing below danger levels.
According to the FFWC, heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected in Rangpur, Sylhet, and Mymensingh divisions, as well as adjoining upstream areas in India's West Bengal, Assam, and Meghalaya.

In the Surma-Kushiyara basin, water levels have risen and may continue to increase over the next three days, potentially causing rivers to flow above danger levels in Sylhet and Sylhet and Sunamganj districts.

Similarly, in the Rangpur Division, the Teesta, Dharla, and Dudhkumar rivers are expected to rise, potentially exceeding danger levels in Nilphamari, Lalmonirhat, Kurigram, and Rangpur districts within 72 hours.
While the Brahmaputra-Jamuna and Ganges-Padma basins are also seeing rising water levels, they are expected to stay below danger marks for the next five days.
The FFWC reported that of 127 monitored water-level stations, readings increased at 56 points, while no station has yet recorded water above the danger level.
Meanwhile, the Sada Pathor tourist spot has been temporarily closed due to heavy rain and upstream runoff.
caption:
